_provenance: Issue #53 family sweep, servicequotas..xray slice (about 115 via:none rows). Evidence for every entry: live/registry.json (the pinned CFN Cloud Control Registry) cross-checked against docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation CloudFormation resource-type reference pages, and hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws's own website/docs markdown for what each TF resource actually manages - both fetched live during this sweep, not recalled from training data.

unclassified (left at via:none, no overlay entry): aws_ses_domain_identity. It is TF's pre-SESv2 (VerifyDomainIdentity, TXT-token) resource for an SES domain identity, the same underlying concept aws_ses_email_identity/aws_sesv2_email_identity already alias to AWS::SES::EmailIdentity - but CFN's EmailIdentity always verifies a domain via DKIM CNAME tokens, never the legacy TXT-record token this resource's own verification_token attribute produces, so the two do not clearly share one verification workflow even though both manage 'an SES identity' in some sense. Considered as an alias to AWS::SES::EmailIdentity (the same 'legacy TF name' shape as the base overlay's aws_cloudwatch_event_rule) and rejected: TestServiceAliasCrossHeuristicCollisions correctly flagged it as colliding with aws_ses_email_identity/aws_sesv2_email_identity, and resolving that would mean asserting the synonym in a test file this fragment should not need to touch. Left genuinely unclassified rather than guessed.

folds (aws_ses_domain_dkim, aws_ses_domain_mail_from, aws_sesv2_email_identity_feedback_attributes, aws_sesv2_email_identity_mail_from_attributes): AWS::SES::EmailIdentity's CFN properties include DkimAttributes/DkimSigningAttributes, MailFromAttributes and FeedbackAttributes (confirmed via its CFN docs page, which live/registry.json's own read/write/create-only buckets don't surface since these are ordinary read-write properties) - TF decomposes each into its own resource.

folds (aws_vpc_endpoint_policy/_private_dns/_route_table_association/_security_group_association/_subnet_association): AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint's CFN properties include PolicyDocument, PrivateDnsEnabled, RouteTableIds, SecurityGroupIds and SubnetIds directly - TF decomposes each into its own resource (aws_vpc_endpoint_private_dns's own docs note it must not be combined with the parent's own DnsOptions to avoid conflicts, confirming the same underlying property).

folds (aws_workspacesweb_*_association, 8 entries): the association between a WorkSpacesWeb Portal and each settings resource is a property on AWS::WorkSpacesWeb::Portal itself (BrowserSettingsArn, DataProtectionSettingsArn, IpAccessSettingsArn, NetworkSettingsArn, SessionLoggerArn, TrustStoreArn, UserAccessLoggingSettingsArn, UserSettingsArn - all confirmed via Portal's CFN docs page), not a property of the settings resource being associated.

tf_only (aws_ses_active_receipt_rule_set, aws_vpc_endpoint_service_private_dns_verification, aws_vpc_ipam_preview_next_cidr): hand-classified rather than caught by mapping.go's mechanical tf-only classifier, since none of their names match its pattern list (accepter/default_/validation/copy/invocation/confirmation/activation/registration) - each is nonetheless a setting, waiter, or dry-run action with no CFN resource of its own per its own provider docs.

cfn_unmodeled (aws_storagegateway_*, 9 entries): live/registry.json's AWS::StorageGateway footprint is exactly one type (TapePool) even though StorageGateway is an active, non-deprecated service - the classic Gateway/CachediSCSIVolume/StorediSCSIVolume/NFSFileShare/SMBFileShare resource-type family was apparently never carried into the Cloud Control Registry snapshot this repo pins. Not classified as deprecated-service (that taxonomy is reserved for live/residue.go's curated, closed DeprecatedServices list, which this sweep does not touch) - the service itself is not deprecated, only unrepresented in the pinned registry.

cfn_unmodeled (aws_workmail_*, 5 entries; aws_swf_domain; aws_servicequotas_*, 4 entries): all three services have zero matching CFN Registry types at all (confirmed by exhaustive substring search over live/registry.json), the same evidence shape as the storagegateway entries above.

unclassified (left at via:none, no overlay entry): aws_vpc_security_group_rules_exclusive. It bulk-reconciles the full set of ingress+egress rules on a security group, spanning both AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupIngress and AWS::EC2::SecurityGroupEgress (the CFN types the base overlay's aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule/egress_rule already alias to) plus AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup's own inline rule properties at once; no single CFN resource or property models that bulk-sync-and-delete-unlisted semantics, and picking one of the three parents by hand would misrepresent what the resource actually does - left genuinely unclassified per the task's own instruction rather than forced into a fold.

service_aliases (timestreamquery, timestreamwrite -> Timestream): namesdata-generated.json lists both as mismatches (AWS SDK ids 'Timestream Query' and 'Timestream Write' don't normalize-match the CFN registry's single 'Timestream' service name). Deliberately NOT adding 'timestreaminfluxdb' here even though it has the same mismatch shape: its two TF types (aws_timestreaminfluxdb_db_cluster/_db_instance) keep 'influx' in both the TF prefix and the CFN resource segment (InfluxDBCluster/InfluxDBInstance), which servicealias.go's cut-point search can never bridge (cutting the whole single-token prefix loses 'influx' entirely) - those two are curated as direct Aliases entries instead, and a service_aliases entry that could never resolve anything would just be dead weight.
